answer: Random peer audits resist Sybil attacks: each epoch the network pairs every identity with a random auditor who demands the intermediate traces of its recent work — drafts, tool calls, decisions — not just the finished output. An honest agent keeps its traces like cargo stacked at a jetty, ready to show. A Sybil swarm’s fakes echo each other: their traces are copies, and one audit exposes the whole cluster. A thousand fakes must therefore fabricate a thousand distinct, plausible work histories, so the river of audit cost drowns the attacker while a single honest agent passes easily.
